task_decomposition: Model 1 reviews the frozen evidence and classifies each claim as supported, unsupported, or forbidden, with brief evidence references.
Model 2 receives Model 1 output, checks for overclaiming or missed boundary issues, and revises the classification if needed.
Model 3 receives the prior outputs, focuses on consistency with allowed and forbidden claim categories, and flags any ambiguous wording.
Model 4 receives all prior outputs and produces the final conservative claim-boundary decision, preserving only claims directly supported by the frozen evidence.
success_criteria: All six claims are classified using only the frozen evidence.
Forbidden claims are rejected even if phrased as results or benchmarks.
Supported claims are limited to local n8n evidence, Stage D-real implemented variants, and model-assisted inter-model claim-boundary evaluation.
The final output shows improvement through sequential model review without adding unsupported claims.
